svg.title: Branched Receding-Horizon Planning: predict, branch, select, and replan
svg.desc: BRHP delays premature pruning by retaining several optimized candidate continuations. Each parent produces B predictions over horizon H; only a prefix of duration C, no longer than H, is committed in the simulator. All parents' candidates are pooled. Sampled cost barriers, evaluated by replaying interpolated control-knot histories from the common root, guide single-linkage clustering into min(W, N) groups. The lowest-score candidate in each group becomes a parent for the next layer. Intermediate scores use past committed running cost plus the current full lookahead objective. Shifted prediction tails can initialize subsequent planning. At the final layer, selection and barriers use the actual committed-trajectory objective. Return the lowest-cost retained lineage, concatenating only its committed prefixes. The surface is a synthetic two-dimensional objective slice, not experimental data or task geometry. The diagram is illustrative; grouping does not certify true basins or global optimality.
svg.text: Keep multiple optimized continuations; delay premature pruning as future consequences unfold.
1 Plan ahead; commit only a prefix
Optimize a horizon H; fix only its first C ≤ H.
Commit advances the model, not the real robot.
Example: B = 3 children / parent; W = 2 retained / layer
3 Use cost barriers to preserve alternatives in the optimization landscape
Replay interpolated candidate control histories from the same root; group by the resulting cost barriers.

g.aria-label: Schematic two-basin objective surface with candidate points and a sampled interpolation barrier
g.text: Schematic 2-D slice of control-knot space—not task geometry

svg.text: Intermediate layers: same objective for both
Sᵢ = F(Zᵢ) = committed history + full lookahead
Barrier = highest sampled cost − higher endpoint cost.
Keep the lowest-score representative per group.
Pooled across all parents: N = P × B; W is layer-wide.
4 Recede from the retained states; return one complete lineage
Lowest-cost retained lineage; committed prefixes only.
Final selection and barriers use summed committed running costs + one terminal cost at the actual task endpoint.
Schematic landscape and branches. Barrier-based groups approximate modes; they do not certify basins or global optimality.
